result.rationale: In parseRefreshTokenResponse, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, the response is parsed against minimumTokenResponseSchema, which only requires access_token (zod strips unknown keys by default). For Salesforce, the parsed data is persisted via prisma.credential.update with key {...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token}, dropping instance_url (and id/signature) that salesforceTokenSchema requires in normal mode. A later jsforce.Connection built from that stored key would lack instance_url, breaking API reachability. Mechanism is verifiable from the diff; severity depends on sharing-mode

adjudication.rationale: In sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse` ignores the provided schema and instead `safeParse`s with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). Because `z.object(...)` is not marked `.passthrough()`, Zod will strip unknown fields from the parsed result. Therefore fields like `instance_url` and `id` from Salesforce’s refresh response will be dropped even if present, and in the Salesforce refresh path the credential is persisted using `accessTokenParsed.data` (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts), causing loss of `instance_url`/`id` needed by jsforce/connection logic.
